correctness.rationale: The multiplication eᵢeⱼ=e₂ⱼ₋ᵢ becomes f(X⁻¹)g(X²) using ordinary group-algebra products only on the right. Truncation below degree five permits the logarithm and exponential identities with invertible denominators, giving the arguments −w and 2w. Expanding the alternating product leaves coefficients 3p₀₁, 3p₀₂, 4(p₀₃+p₁₂), and 4p₁₃; the degree-four pair (0,4) cancels since 2⁴−1=0 in characteristic five. The single Plücker equation is sufficient: pivot on any nonzero minor and reconstruct two rows, with the equation ensuring the remaining minor. When a=z₁/3 is nonzero one can solve for p₂₃; otherwise the equation is u²−su+bd=0 for b=z₂/3, s=z₃/4, d=z₄/4. Its discriminant is the stated z₃²−2z₂z₄, with zero permitted. The four monomial basis vectors of the augmentation ideal are scalar multiples of commutators and the ideal is closed under the native multiplication. Every zero-leading vector is w+(z−w), while a nonsquare δ obstructs z₂=1, z₄=−δ/2, z₁=z₃=0. For q=5^m the obstruction has z₁=0 and z₂≠0; independently choose z₂, z₃ and one of (q−1)/2 nonsquares to determine z₄ uniquely, giving the count and the length partition.
residual_risks: Finite checking over F₅ and the reported tests over F₂₅ are corroboration only; the arbitrary-field result rests on the Plücker and quadratic arguments. The claim does not concern the commutator in the associative model or other dihedral orders.

evidence: Zhang's generated-subalgebra theorem for Alexander quandle rings specializes to the augmentation ideal for the core of Z/5: φ=−1 and 1−2φ=3 is invertible.
The earlier general width framework does not give the exact R₅ pointwise characterization. The distinct exact catalogue result does so for the whole field class at issue.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Equality of the generated subalgebra with the augmentation ideal is also a specialization of broader work, but it does not by itself characterize the image of the two-input commutator map. The exact catalogue theorem closes that gap already.

evidence: The catalogue proof uses the same Plücker condition and the same quadratic, gives the identical width-one/two dichotomy, and counts the nonsquare fibers.
Zhang's theorem only describes the generated subalgebra, not individual commutators.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The catalogue includes the supposed geometric explanation as well as the conclusions. Presenting the length-two fraction or distinguishing zero from the nonzero single values does not produce a substantive remaining theorem.

value.rationale: A pointwise criterion for an entire natural field class would be useful if not already available. This package offers the same criterion, the same Plücker derivation, and the same counts as the matching indexed result. Its finite corroboration and complementary counts do not provide an additional structural fact, different proof, or useful new family to justify it as a distinct scientific contribution.
residual_risks: This does not deny the mathematical usefulness of the criterion itself; it concerns the marginal value of the submitted contribution. No distinct surviving claim was identified for repair.
